'''Mary Ellen Johnston Bock''' is a retired American statistician, now a professor emeritus at [[Purdue University]]{{r|profile}}
after becoming the first female full professor of statistics and the first female chair of the department there.{{r|sin}}
She was [[president of the American Statistical Association]] in 2007.{{r|aws}}

==Education and career==
As an undergraduate at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], Bock earned a bachelor's degree in the [[German language]] in 1967.{{r|profile}} She switched to mathematics for her graduate studies at the same university, completing her PhD in 1974 under the supervision of Robert B. Ash with a dissertation on ''Certain Minimax Estimators of the Mean of a Multivariate Normal Distribution''.{{r|profile|mgp}}<ref>{{cite journal |author = M. E. Bock |title=Minimax Estimators of the Mean of a Multivariate Normal Distribution |journal=Ann. Statist. |date=January 1975 |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=209–218 |doi=10.1214/aos/1176343009  |doi-access=free }}</ref>

As chair of statistics at Purdue from 1995 to 2010, Bock led the department through a period of growth, and took a multidisciplinary approach to the subject that included [[computational statistics]] as well as application areas including [[biostatistics]], [[statistical finance]], and [[environmental statistics]].{{r|sin}}

==Awards and honors==
Bock is a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],{{r|profile}} and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|fims}} She won the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]] in 2013.{{r|profile}}
